war_stories.summary: fix(mandi): reserve the whole ad block to hold CLS down
war_stories.body:
CLS measured 0.093-0.099 across mandi page types — inside the 0.1 'good'
threshold, but close enough that one taller creative would cross it.

Only the <ins> carried a min-height, so the label above it claimed its height at
fill time. The wrapper now reserves 300px (280 for the unit, the rest for the
label) with contain:layout, so nothing below the ad can be pushed by it.

war_stories.summary: fix(mandi,a11y): paint the page canvas and add a main landmark
war_stories.body:
Lighthouse scored these 99 / 95 / 77 / 100. Both accessibility failures were
mine.

color-contrast reported #f1f5f9 text on #ffffff — a ratio of 1.09, effectively
invisible. That is the dark-mode foreground on the light-mode background: only
.mandi carried a background, and it is a centred max-width box, so under
prefers-color-scheme: dark the variables went light while the page canvas stayed
the browser default white. html and body now carry the background too, so
foreground and background can no longer come from different schemes. Light mode
was always correct, which is why opening the page by hand did not show it.

landmark-one-main: the pages had no <main> at all. The .mandi wrapper is the
main content, so it is now a <main> rather than a <div>.

The two remaining Best Practices failures are third-party-cookies and
inspector-issues, both from AdSense cookies, and cap that category at 77 on
every page of this site regardless of framework.

war_stories.summary: fix(mandi): self-contained pages, real ad inventory, capped tables
war_stories.body:
Three problems with the first cut, all found by opening the pages rather than
trusting the build.

The pages reused build/index.html as their template, so each carried ~16KB of
React app shell they cannot use — critical CSS extracted for a layout they do
not have, deferred stylesheet links, the Translate and PerformanceObserver
bootstraps, preconnects for bundles that get stripped anyway. Across 7,000 pages
that was 111MB, committed to the build branch every night. They now emit a
purpose-built document: metadata, their own stylesheet, the ad loader, nothing
else.

  mandi HTML  111MB -> 56MB      build total 139MB -> 84MB

They shipped with no ads at all. The loader was being regex-extracted from
build/index.html, and by that point in the build it is minified onto one line,
so a pattern written against the source matched nothing — silently, with the
build still green. It is now written out explicitly, along with an <ins> and its
push, because these pages ship no React and AdUnit never runs. 7,035 pages that
carried zero inventory now carry a slot.

National commodity pages listed every reporting market — 171 rows for onion,
which is both an unreadable table and the largest page in the build. Capped at
40 with a line saying how many were omitted and where the rest are; state pages
still carry their complete list.

Coverage turned out far better than the morning snapshot suggested. The feed
grows through the day as mandis report: 236 rows and 59 markets at 08:30 IST,
6,395 rows and 359 markets by 10:30. Dispersion falls with the larger sample
too — onion 36% -> 20%, tomato 45% -> 23%, brinjal 101% -> 43% — so the earlier
figures were small-sample noise, not real volatility. 415 pages became 7,035.

raw_readme:
# TodayEggRates — Developer Quickstart

A minimal developer guide for the TodayEggRates project.

Purpose: quickly get the app running, know where key code lives, and how to validate changes.

## Quick commands (PowerShell, run from repo root)

Install deps

```powershell
npm install
```

Run dev server (frontend) — prestart regenerates blogs

```powershell
npm start
```

Build production bundle (runs image + blog pipelines)

```powershell
npm run build
```

Regenerate blog artifacts (when editing MDX source)

```powershell
node scripts/build-blog-index.js
```

Optimize images

```powershell
npm run optimize-images
```

## Where the important code is

- Frontend React: `src/` (entry: `src/index.js`, `src/App.js`).
- API client: `src/services/api.js` (enhancedFetch, postRequest).
- Generated blog components: `src/blogs/` (do NOT edit directly).
- Blog sources: `blogs_source/` (edit MDX here; run `build-blog-index.js`).
- Image pipeline: `scripts/optimize-images.js` → outputs to `public/optimized/`.
- PHP backend & cron: `public/php/` (APIs: `public/php/api/`, cron: `public/php/cron/`).
- Build config & aliasing: `webpack.config.js`, `config-overrides.js` (`@/` → `src/`).

## Quick validation

- Smoke UI: `npm install; npm start` and open the dev server.
- Production check: `npm run build` (watch for build errors/warnings).
- Blog changes: run `node scripts/build-blog-index.js` and confirm `src/blogs/index.json`.
- Image changes: run `npm run optimize-images` and inspect `public/optimized/`.
- Test backend endpoints via the local PHP server above; check `public/php/error.log` for server-side errors.

## Security notes

- Never commit production DB credentials or admin tokens. Move secrets to environment-backed config (example files or env vars) and exclude real credentials from Git.
- Protect admin/write APIs with server-side auth (API keys, sessions, IP allowlist) and validate/sanitize inputs in PHP endpoints.

## Where to look first

- API client: `src/services/api.js`
- Routing & app boot: `src/App.js`
- Blog pipeline: `scripts/build-blog-index.js` and `blogs_source/`
- PHP APIs: `public/php/api/`

Need more details or a specific smoke-test script? Tell me which endpoints or pages to cover and I will add a tiny test harness or examples.
